question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The main affect B. of the new policy C. will be an increase D. in productivity.
option_2: of the new policy
option_4: in productivity
solution_text:
The correct answer is The main affect.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the word 'affect'. Here the noun form is required, and the correct noun is 'effect' (meaning result/outcome), not the verb 'affect' (to influence). The sentence should read 'The main effect of the new policy will be an increase in productivity.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• 'Affect' is usually a verb meaning 'to influence' (e.g., The weather affected our plans). 'Effect' is usually a noun meaning 'a result' (e.g., The effect was immediate). This affect/effect confusion is a very common SSC error-spotting trap.

 

NOTE

• Parts B ('of the new policy'), C ('will be an increase') and D ('in productivity') are all grammatically correct and contain no error.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:

His promotion was contingent ______ the outcome of the annual review.
option_2: to
option_4: into
solution_text:
The correct answer is on.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective 'contingent' collocates with the preposition 'on' (or 'upon'). 'Contingent on' means 'depending on / conditional upon'. Thus, 'His promotion was contingent on the outcome of the annual review.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Fixed collocation: contingent on/upon = subject to a condition. Similar dependency prepositions: 'dependent on', 'reliant on', 'conditional on'. SSC frequently tests such adjective + preposition pairings.

 

NOTE

• 'upto' (Option 1) is not a standard single word and does not fit. 'to' (Option 2) and 'into' (Option 4) are not used with 'contingent'.

question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: TRANSHISTORICAL
option_2: Ancient
option_4: Futuristic
solution_text:
The correct answer is Timeless.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Transhistorical' means transcending or extending beyond the bounds of history, i.e., something not limited to a particular period — essentially 'timeless'. Hence 'Timeless' is the closest synonym.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• The prefix 'trans-' means 'across/beyond'. Transhistorical = beyond/across history. Synonyms: timeless, eternal, universal, ageless.

 

NOTE

• 'Ancient' and 'Recent' both tie the meaning to a specific time period, which is opposite to 'beyond history'. 'Futuristic' relates only to the future, so it is also incorrect.

question: Choose the correctly spelt word
option_2: Extroversoin
option_4: Extroversin
solution_text:
The correct answer is Extroversion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the psychological term is 'Extroversion' (the state of being outgoing/directing attention outward). The remaining options are misspellings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Root: 'extro-/extra-' (outward) + 'version' (turning). Antonym: 'Introversion'. Related word: 'Extrovert'. SSC spelling questions reward knowing common suffix patterns like '-sion'.

 

NOTE

• 'Extroversoin', 'Extroverssion' and 'Extroversin' are all incorrect spellings (transposed/duplicated/omitted letters).

question:
Which of the following sentences uses the word "minute" with the same meaning as in the following sentence?

"The microscope revealed a minute speck of dust"
option_1: The meeting will start in a few minutes
option_2: I was just a minute away from being late.
option_3: The camera captured every minute detail of the insect's wing.
option_4: The alarm went off in exactly sixty seconds, or one minute.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The camera captured every minute detail of the insect's wing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the given sentence, 'minute' (pronounced my-NEWT) is an adjective meaning 'extremely small/tiny'. Only Option 3 uses 'minute' with this same meaning — 'every minute detail' = every tiny detail.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• 'minute' is a homograph: as a noun (MIN-it) it means a unit of time; as an adjective (my-NEWT) it means very small. Synonyms of the adjective: tiny, minuscule, microscopic.

 

NOTE

• Options 1, 2 and 4 all use 'minute(s)' as the time-unit noun, which is a different meaning from the tiny-size adjective in the given sentence.

question: Choose the correctly spelt word
option_2: Busyness
option_4: Buseness
solution_text:
The correct answer is Business.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the word meaning trade/commerce or one's occupation is 'Business'. The others are misspellings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• 'Business' = busi + ness. Note that 'Busyness' is a real but different word meaning 'the state of being busy'; in the context of a spelling test for the common word, 'Business' is intended.

 

NOTE

• 'Bussiness' and 'Buseness' are clearly wrong spellings. 'Busyness' is a distinct rarer word and is not the standard spelling of the commerce word.

question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it:

The idea of progress has always gone hand in hand with the evolution of human beings and the invention of technology. Each technological revolution has unearthed revolutionary changes that have rewritten the human experience in the past. From the invention of the printing press to the invention of the internet, technological breakthroughs have shaped the manner in which we live, work, and communicate. But with our arrival in an age of artificial intelligence, automation, and biotechnology comes a growing paradox: while these technologies offer unparalleled convenience and power, they also undermine tried-and-true social forms and erode the very notion of what it means to be human. Technological advances, first of all, have provided standards of living much better. Medical advances like gene editing and precision medicine hold the promise to cure diseases that were once thought incurable. Communication technology has made the world think alike in ways that people could not have imagined a couple of decades ago, with people able to work together across borders and cultures with relative ease. But the same technology has profound implications. Automation is taking away jobs for millions of people, particularly where human labor can be automated. The speed of innovation has left millions behind, and with it there is a feeling of disconnection, fear for the future. Secondly, our dependence on technology is creating basic questions regarding privacy, security, and freedom. As we introduce AI into everyday life, do we have to sit back and ask ourselves: are we Master of Technology, or is technology the master of us? The paradox of progress, then, is in its double-edged nature. On one hand, technology comes bearing answers to some of humankind's biggest problems, yet it also brings new issues that human beings must resolve in order to make progress mean a more just and sustainable tomorrow.

 

What is the main paradox introduced in the passage regarding technological advancements?
option_1: Technology always improves the quality of life
option_2: Technology eliminates all forms of labor
option_3: Technology offers convenience but also undermines social structures and the notion of being human
option_4: Technology solves all human problems without consequences
solution_text:
The correct answer is Technology offers convenience but also undermines social structures and the notion of being human.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage explicitly states the 'growing paradox: while these technologies offer unparalleled convenience and power, they also undermine tried-and-true social forms and erode the very notion of what it means to be human.' Option 3 restates this exactly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A 'paradox' is a statement/situation combining two seemingly contradictory truths. Look for signal words like 'but', 'while', 'yet', 'double-edged' to locate a paradox in RC passages.

 

NOTE

• Options 1 and 4 are one-sided positive claims the passage never makes. Option 2 ('eliminates all forms of labor') overstates and misreads 'automation is taking away jobs'.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: Part and parce
option_2: A non-essential part of a whole
option_4: A delivery service for packages
solution_text:
The correct answer is An integral and unavoidable component.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom 'part and parcel' means an essential, integral and inseparable part of something. Hence 'An integral and unavoidable component' is the correct meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Usage: 'Long hours are part and parcel of a doctor's job.' Synonymous idea: 'an inherent/inseparable element'.

 

NOTE

• Options 1 and 2 wrongly suggest something minor or non-essential, which is the opposite meaning. Option 4 is a literal misreading of the word 'parcel'.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Credulous
option_2: Skeptical
option_4: Naive
solution_text:
The correct answer is Skeptical.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Credulous' means too ready to believe things; gullible. Its antonym is 'Skeptical', meaning inclined to doubt or question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Root 'cred-' means 'believe' (credible, credit, creed). Synonyms of credulous: gullible, naive, trusting. Antonyms: skeptical, incredulous, suspicious.

 

NOTE

• 'Trusting' (Option 1), 'Gullible' (Option 3) and 'Naive' (Option 4) are all synonyms of 'credulous', not antonyms.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

The killing of one's own mother.
option_2: Patricide
option_4: Fratricide
solution_text:
The correct answer is Matricide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Matricide' is the killing of one's own mother. The root 'matri-' means mother.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Related '-cide' (kill) words: Patricide = killing one's father; Fratricide = killing one's brother; Sororicide = killing one's sister; Homicide = killing of a human; Regicide = killing a king; Infanticide = killing an infant.

 

NOTE

• Patricide (father), Homicide (a human being in general) and Fratricide (brother) do not refer to killing one's mother.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A large-scale departure of people from one place
option_2: Emigration
option_4: Migration
solution_text:
The correct answer is Exodus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Exodus' means a mass/large-scale departure of people from a place. It best captures 'a large-scale departure of people from one place'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Emigration = leaving one's own country to settle in another; Immigration = coming into a new country to settle; Migration = seasonal or general movement of people/animals. 'Exodus' specifically stresses a large, mass departure.

 

NOTE

• Emigration, Immigration and Migration describe types of movement but do not specifically denote a large-scale mass departure the way 'Exodus' does.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

A new bridge is being constructed by the city council.
option_1: The city council is constructing a new bridge
option_2: A new bridge constructed the city council.
option_3: The city council constructed a new bridge.
option_4: The city council has constructed a new bridge.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The city council is constructing a new bridge.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passive sentence is in present continuous tense ('is being constructed'). Its active form must also be present continuous: subject 'The city council' + is + constructing + object 'a new bridge'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Present continuous passive 'is/are being + V3' converts to active 'is/are + V-ing'. Keep the tense unchanged when changing voice.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 is illogical (bridge cannot construct the council). Options 3 and 4 wrongly shift the tense to simple past and present perfect respectively.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Ineffable
option_2: Inarticulate
option_4: Indescribable
solution_text:
The correct answer is Expressible.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Ineffable' means too great or extreme to be expressed in words; indescribable. Its antonym is 'Expressible', meaning able to be expressed/put into words.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Prefix 'in-' = not; 'effable' = able to be uttered. Synonyms of ineffable: indescribable, inexpressible, unspeakable. Antonyms: expressible, describable, definable.

 

NOTE

• 'Inarticulate' (Option 2) means unable to speak clearly and is not an antonym. 'Unfathomable' (Option 3) and 'Indescribable' (Option 4) are synonyms of 'ineffable', not antonyms.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

The manager said, "We will make a decision by Friday."
option_1: The manager said that they would make a decision by Friday.
option_2: The manager said that we would make a decision by Friday.
option_3: The manager said that they will make a decision by Friday
option_4: The manager said that we will make a decision by Friday
solution_text:
The correct answer is The manager said that they would make a decision by Friday.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In indirect speech, the reporting verb 'said' (past) shifts 'will' to 'would', and the pronoun 'we' changes to 'they' (referring to the manager's group). Hence: 'The manager said that they would make a decision by Friday.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Backshift rules: will → would, can → could, may → might. Pronouns change according to sense; here first-person 'we' becomes third-person 'they'.

 

NOTE

• Options 2 and 4 wrongly keep 'we'. Options 3 and 4 wrongly keep 'will' instead of backshifting to 'would'.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

Twenty minutes has been the time I need to get ready for the party.
option_2: Twenty minutes is the time
option_4: Twenty minutes are the time needed
solution_text:
The correct answer is Twenty minutes is the time.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A measure of time like 'twenty minutes' is treated as a single/whole unit and takes a singular verb. Therefore 'Twenty minutes is the time' is correct (not 'has been'/'are').

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rule: Expressions of distance, time, money and weight taken as one unit take a singular verb (e.g., 'Ten kilometres is a long way', 'Five hundred rupees is enough').

 

NOTE

• Options 1 and 4 use the plural verb 'are'. Option 3 wrongly uses singular 'minute' with the numeral 'Twenty'.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

Necessity being the mother of invention, he resourcefully modifies the Rover to go on long drives even though it have originally designed for short one.
option_1: it has originally have been designed for short one
option_2: it has originally been designed for short ones
option_3: it has originally was designed for short ones
option_4: it has originally has been designed to short one
solution_text:
The correct answer is it has originally been designed for short ones.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause needs a present perfect passive: 'has been designed'. Correct form: 'it has originally been designed for short ones', which is grammatical and agrees in number ('drives' → 'short ones').

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Present perfect passive structure: has/have + been + V3. Adverb 'originally' is correctly placed between 'has' and 'been'.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 ('has originally have been') and Option 4 ('has ... has been') have double auxiliaries. Option 3 ('has ... was designed') mixes perfect and past incorrectly and Option 4 also wrongly uses 'to short one'.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

The renowned author's newest novel will have been released by the end of the year.
option_1: The renowned author will have been releasing his newest novel by the end of the year.
option_2: The renowned author will release his newest novel by the end of the year.
option_3: The renowned author will have released his newest novel by the end of the year.
option_4: The renowned author has released his newest novel by the end of the year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The renowned author will have released his newest novel by the end of the year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given passive is in future perfect ('will have been released'). Its active form must be future perfect active: 'will have + V3'. Thus: 'The renowned author will have released his newest novel by the end of the year.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Future perfect passive 'will have been + V3' ↔ active 'will have + V3'. The object of the passive ('novel') becomes the object in active with the doer 'author' as subject.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 wrongly uses continuous 'been releasing'. Option 2 uses simple future and Option 4 uses present perfect — both change the tense incorrectly.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

You should have kept us informed about the progress of the investigation.
option_1: We should be kept informed about the progress of the investigation by you.
option_2: We should have been kept informed about the progress of the investigation by you
option_3: We should have been keeping informed about the progress of the investigation by you.
option_4: We should have kept informed about the progress of the investigation by you.
solution_text:
The correct answer is We should have been kept informed about the progress of the investigation by you.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The active 'should have kept' (perfect modal) converts to passive as 'should have been kept'. The object 'us' becomes subject 'We', and the agent 'you' is added: 'We should have been kept informed ... by you.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Modal perfect passive: should/could/would + have been + V3. Here 'kept' (V3) is retained.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 drops 'have been'. Option 3 uses 'keeping' (continuous). Option 4 omits 'been', giving 'should have kept', which is incorrect passive.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.

The manager told the team that their hard work and dedication had been noticed and appreciated.
option_1: The manager said, "Your hard work and dedication had been noticed and appreciated.'
option_2: The manager said, "Your hard work and dedication have been noticed and appreciated."
option_3: The manager told the team, "Their hard work and dedication had been noticed and appreciated."
option_4: The manager said, "Their hard work and dedication were noticed and appreciated."
solution_text:
The correct answer is The manager said, "Your hard work and dedication have been noticed and appreciated."

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Converting to direct speech, 'their' addressed to the team becomes 'Your', and the backshifted past perfect 'had been' returns to present perfect 'have been'. Hence: The manager said, "Your hard work and dedication have been noticed and appreciated."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Reverse backshift in direct speech: had been → have been; third-person pronouns addressed to listeners → 'you/your'. Quotation marks and correct punctuation are required.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 keeps 'had been' and has a mismatched closing quote. Option 3 keeps 'Their' (should be 'Your') and 'had been'. Option 4 wrongly changes the verb to 'were noticed'.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.

He asked me if I would have been able to finish the report that day if he had not helped me with the research, which had been a very tedious process.
option_1: "Would you have been able to finish the report today if I had not helped you with the research, which was a very tedious process?" he asked me.
option_2: "Will you have been able to finish the report today if I did not help you with the research, which was a very tedious process?" he asked me.
option_3: "Would you have been able to finish the report that day if I had not helped you with the research, which had been a very tedious process?" he asked me.
option_4: "Could you finish the report today if I had not helped you with the research, which was a very tedious process?" he asked me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is "Would you have been able to finish the report today if I had not helped you with the research, which was a very tedious process?" he asked me.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the official answer key, Option 1 is marked correct. In converting to direct speech, 'that day' returns to 'today', pronouns shift ('I' → 'you', 'he' → 'I'), and the reporting turns into an interrogative with quotation marks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Reverse backshift for direct speech: that day → today, and question form restored with '?'. The conditional 'would have been able' is retained in the direct question.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 wrongly uses 'Will' and 'did not help'. Option 3 keeps 'that day' and 'had been' (not converted to direct form). Option 4 changes the structure to 'Could you finish', altering the meaning.

question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. She created a decadent batter and baked three layers of cake flawlessly.

Q. The finished cake was a stunning design, prepared for the celebration and the candles.

R. She coated the outside of the entire cake after stacking the layers with icing between them.

S. Before gently levelling each cake layer, she created a light and creamy icing.
option_2: P, S, R, Q
option_4: R, S, P, Q
solution_text:
The correct answer is P, S, R, Q.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The logical baking sequence is: P (make batter and bake the layers) → S (level the layers and make the icing) → R (stack the layers and coat the outside) → Q (the finished cake is ready). This gives P, S, R, Q.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• For para-jumble/sentence-rearrangement, follow the natural chronological process and track referential clues (e.g., 'each cake layer', 'the entire cake', 'the finished cake').

 

NOTE

• Sequences beginning with S, Q or R (Options 1, 3, 4) break the process order — the paragraph must start with baking the layers (P) before levelling, stacking or describing the finished cake.
